questions.question: In the question given below, a statement is followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. You have to consider the statement and decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement. Statement: Children should not play games on mobile phone for the whole day. Assumption: I. It can result in digital eyestrain. II. It has bad effect on study.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question given below, a statement is followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. You have to consider the statement and decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.

Statement:

 Children should not play games on mobile phone for the whole day.

Assumption:

I. It can result in digital eyestrain.

II. It has bad effect on study.

options.text: If only assumption I is implicit
options.html: If only assumption I is implicit

options.text: If only assumption II is implicit
options.html: If only assumption II is implicit

options.text: If neither I or II is implicit
options.html: If neither I or II is implicit

options.text: If both I and II are implicit
options.html: If both I and II are implicit

questions.solution:
Given:

Statement: Children should not play games on mobile phone for the whole day.

Assumptions:

I. It can result in digital eyestrain - True (Because advising children not to play mobile games for the whole day implies that prolonged screen time may have harmful effects, such as digital eyestrain.)

II. It has bad effect on study - True (Because the advice also assumes that spending the whole day playing mobile games can negatively affect children's studies by reducing the time and attention devoted to learning.)

So, both Assumptions I and II are implicit.

Hence, the correct answer is "Both Assumptions I and II are implicit."

questions.question: If 8@3 = 10, 9@1 = 16 and 5@4 = 2, then what is the value of 7@3 = ?
questions.questionHtml: If 8@3 = 10, 9@1 = 16 and 5@4 = 2, then what is the value of 7@3 = ?
questions.solution:
The logic is:

8@3 = 10 → (8 - 3) × 2 = 10

9@1 = 16 → (9 - 1) × 2 = 16

5@4 = 2 → (5 - 4) × 2 = 2

Similarly,

7@ 3 = ? → (7 - 3) × 2 = 8

Hence, ‘8’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a class examination, among the students who passed, a student’s rank is 26th from the left and 19th from the right. If 7 students failed the examination, find the total number of students in the class.
questions.questionHtml: In a class examination, among the students who passed, a student’s rank is 26th from the left and 19th from the right. If 7 students failed the examination, find the total number of students in the class.
questions.solution:
Student’s rank from right = 19

Student’s rank from left = 26
Total passed students = Student’s rank from right + Student’s rank from left - 1

→ 19 + 26 - 1

→ 44

Passed students = 44

Failed students = 7

Thus, total students = 44 + 7

→ 51

Hence, the total number of students is 51.

questions.question: Read the following statement and answer. Which of the following arguments is stronger? Statement: Should candidates be barred from contesting elections if criminal charges are pending against them in a court of law? Argument: 1. Yes, these people should not be allowed to contest elections, because they have already violated the law, if they are elected then the violations will continue at a fast pace. 2. No, they are authorized to contest elections by the respective political parties.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement and answer. Which of the following arguments is stronger?

Statement: Should candidates be barred from contesting elections if criminal charges are pending against them in a court of law?

Argument: 

1. Yes, these people should not be allowed to contest elections, because they have already violated the law, if they are elected then the violations will continue at a fast pace.

2. No, they are authorized to contest elections by the respective political parties.

options.text: Both argument 1 and argument 2 are strong.
options.html: Both argument 1 and argument 2 are strong.

options.text: Neither argument 1 nor argument 2 is strong.
options.html: Neither argument 1 nor argument 2 is strong.

questions.solution:
Statement: 

Should candidates be barred from contesting elections if criminal charges are pending against them in a court of law?

Argument:

Argument 1 is weak because it violates the legal principle of "innocent until proven guilty." Since the statement specifies the charges are only "pending," assuming they have "already violated the law" is a logical fallacy. Furthermore, claiming violations will continue at a "fast pace" is speculative, not a factual consequence.

Argument 2 is weak because it is circular and irrelevant to the ethical/legal question. The fact that political parties authorize them does not address whether they should be barred by law; it merely describes the current situation rather than providing a strong reason for or against the change.

Hence, "Neither argument 1 nor argument 2 is strong".

questions.solution:
Given Statement: M ≥ N < O = P > Q > R > S

Now, Conclusions:

Option 1: M > Q → False (M ≥ N < O = P > Q, It gives M < Q or M = Q)

Option 2: O > R → True (O = P > Q > R, It gives O > R)

So, Only conclusion II is true.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Directions: Answer the question given below You see that your senior manager is taking bribes from customers to get their work done. As his junior, what will you do?
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Answer the question given below

You see that your senior manager is taking bribes from customers to get their work done. As his junior, what will you do?

options.text: Get a proof of him taking the bribe and submit it to the police.
options.html: Get a proof of him taking the bribe and submit it to the police.

options.text: Ignore that he is taking bribe because he is your senior.
options.html: Ignore that he is taking bribe because he is your senior.

options.text: Make a note of the customers he takes bribe from and return the money to them.
options.html: Make a note of the customers he takes bribe from and return the money to them.

options.text: Inform his senior about the situation and ask them to take appropriate action.
options.html: Inform his senior about the situation and ask them to take appropriate action.

questions.solution:
Even if the person is your senior manager, he is committing a crime. So it is necessary to take action against him.

However, since he is your senior, it is advised that someone of higher authority than him takes action on the matter. Hence, it is appropriate to inform his senior and let him take the necessary action.

Hence the correct answer is Option 4
